findings.title: Upload URL pattern exceeds Rule 1 scope
findings.problem: ATTACHMENT_UPLOAD_URL_PATTERN r'/child/attachment(/\d+/data)?/?$' also treats PUT .../attachment/{id}/data as an upload, which Rule 1 does not list, while \d+ will not match real Confluence attachment ids such as 'att123', so the update form falls through to a plain request. Tests only use a numeric id.
findings.impact: Attachment-update PUTs with real ids bypass the file handling while numeric ones are intercepted; behavior diverges from the spec on a live path.
findings.recommendation: Make the pattern match Rule 1 and decide explicitly on the /{id}/data form with a non-digit-only id (e.g. [^/]+); add tests using a real attachment id.
findings.check_notes: Pattern now /child/attachment/?(\?.*)?$; the /{id}/data update form is no longer an upload, so ids like att123 are consistent; tests cover both.

fix.change: Upload pattern narrowed to POST/PUT .../child/attachment; /{id}/data update form no longer intercepted

findings.title: Same-name attach versioning unverified
findings.problem: Spec Rule 10 requires that attaching a same-named file adds a new version, verified against the installed atlassian library. No code, test or note settles same-name versioning, request timeout or the update URL for confluence.attach_content.
findings.impact: A required spec behavior is partial; re-attaching a regenerated JSON may fail or behave differently than specified.
findings.recommendation: Verify attach_content behavior with an existing name in the installed atlassian library, add a test or documented note settling Rule 10.
findings.check_notes: New test pins atlassian attach_content behavior; installed library source confirms filename lookup and POST to .../{id}/data (new version).

fix.change: Rule 10 settled: installed atlassian attach_content looks up same-name attachment and posts a new version to /{id}/data; pinned by a test

findings.title: Size 0/None row bypasses size limit
findings.problem: read_generated checks info.size, built as row.size or 0; a row with missing size but a large blob skips the limit check and is fully read.
findings.impact: Trigger is narrow: only workspace rows lacking a stored size; no workaround needed otherwise.
findings.recommendation: Also check len(content) against the limit after read.
findings.check_notes: Post-read len(data) limit check added with test.

fix.change: read_generated also checks len(content) against the limit

disposition.rationale: user chose to fix all 7 findings now

findings.title: Naive vs aware datetime in newest-wins
findings.problem: max(generated, key=lambda c: c.updated or datetime.min) mixes naive datetime.min with possibly tz-aware updated values.
findings.impact: TypeError only when same-name duplicates mix a None update date with a tz-aware one; whether update_date is tz-aware was unconfirmed.
findings.recommendation: Use key=lambda c: c.updated.timestamp() if c.updated else float('-inf').
findings.check_notes: Key uses timestamp() or -inf; mixed naive/aware test added.

fix.change: newest-wins key uses timestamp, missing date ranks oldest

findings.title: Query string on upload URL skips upload path
findings.problem: The pattern is anchored with $ and does not allow a query string such as ?allowDuplicated=true.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger: model appends a query string; request falls through to a plain POST. Reachability unconfirmed.
findings.check_notes: Optional query suffix allowed in pattern; test added.

findings.title: Candidate listing errors escape raw
findings.problem: _attachment_candidates() calls source.list_generated() outside any try block in _handle_file_attachments.
findings.impact: A repository/DB failure surfaces as a raw exception instead of a clear attachment ToolException; rare trigger.
findings.recommendation: Wrap in try/except Exception and raise ToolException from e.
findings.check_notes: Listing wrapped, raises ToolException; test added.

findings.title: Repeated file name attaches twice
findings.problem: A files list repeating a name is not de-duplicated, so the same file is attached twice.
findings.impact: Creates a duplicate attachment version; only when the model repeats a name.
findings.check_notes: Names de-duplicated with dict.fromkeys; test added.
